title: Activation checkpointing skips RNG state preservation even when dropout is active — backward recomputes a different mask
trigger_conditions: nn.Dropout module present in the model graph (dropout > 0)
root_cause: Transformer.apply_activation_checkpointing hard-coded preserve_rng_state=False with a TODO. With dropout active, the recomputed forward in backward used a fresh random mask, so backward gradients corresponded to a different forward graph than the one used to produce the loss — silently wrong gradients and degraded convergence.
invariant: If any nn.Dropout module exists, the forward run during backward recompute must use the same RNG state as the original forward (preserve_rng_state=True).
diff_summary: Set preserve_rng_state = any(isinstance(m, nn.Dropout) for m in self.modules()) so checkpointing pins the RNG state when dropout is active.
